questions.question: A 1000 kg car moving at 10 m/s is brought to rest by a constant braking force in 5 s. What is the magnitude of the force?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2000 N**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The mass of the car is given as **1000 kg**. 
 
• The initial velocity of the car is **10 m/s**, and the final velocity is **0 m/s** (since it is brought to rest). 
 
• The time taken to bring the car to rest is given as **5 seconds**. 
 
• Using the formula for acceleration: **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, and **t** is the time: 
 **a = (0 - 10) / 5 = -2 m/s²** (negative sign indicates deceleration). 
 
• The braking force can be calculated using Newton's second law of motion: **F = m × a**, where **m** is the mass and **a** is the acceleration: 
 **F = 1000 × (-2) = -2000 N**. The negative sign indicates the direction of the force is opposite to the motion, but the magnitude is **2000 N**.
 
• **Hence, the magnitude of the braking force is 2000 N.** 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion:** 
 
 
• It states that the force acting on an object is equal to the mass of the object multiplied by its acceleration: **F = m × a**. 
 
• This law explains how the velocity of an object changes when it is subjected to an external force. 
 
 
 
• **Acceleration:** 
 
 
• It is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time. 
 
• It can be calculated using the formula: **a = (v - u) / t**, where **v** is the final velocity, **u** is the initial velocity, and **t** is the time. 
 
 
 
• **Braking Force:** 
 
 
• It is the force applied to bring a moving object to rest or reduce its velocity. 
 
• In this case, the braking force is calculated using Newton's second law, considering the deceleration of the car. 
 
 
 
• **Practical Applications:** 
 
 
• Understanding braking force is crucial in designing braking systems for vehicles to ensure safety and efficiency. 
 
• It is also used in calculating stopping distances and improving road safety features. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Force:** It is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction. 
 
• **Unit of Force:** The SI unit of force is the **Newton (N)**, where 1 N = 1 kg·m/s². 
 
• **Deceleration:** A negative acceleration value indicates a reduction in velocity or slowing down. 
 
• **Stopping Distance:** The distance required to bring a moving vehicle to rest depends on the initial velocity, braking force, and road conditions.

questions.question: A concave mirror forms an image at a distance of 20 cm when an object is placed 10 cm in front of it. What is the focal length of this mirror?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 cm**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To solve this question, we use the **mirror formula**: 
 **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**, where:
 
 
• **f** is the focal length of the mirror.
 
• **v** is the distance of the image from the mirror.
 
• **u** is the distance of the object from the mirror.
 
 
 
• Given:
 
 
• **v = 20 cm** (image distance).
 
• **u = -10 cm** (object distance; negative because the object is placed on the same side as the reflecting surface).
 
 
 
• Using the formula:
 
 
• **1/f = 1/v + 1/u**
 
• Substitute the values: **1/f = 1/20 + 1/(-10)**
 
• **1/f = 1/20 - 1/10**
 
• Find the LCM: **1/f = (1 - 2)/20 = -1/20**
 
• Thus, **f = -20 cm**.
 
 
 
• The negative sign indicates that the focal length is on the same side as the object, confirming it is a **concave mirror**.
 
• **Therefore, the focal length of the mirror is 20 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mirror Formula:**
 
 
• The formula **1/f = 1/v + 1/u** is universally applicable for all mirrors (concave, convex, or plane).
 
• It relates the focal length (**f**), object distance (**u**), and image distance (**v**).
 
• Sign convention is crucial:
 
 
• Distances measured in the direction of the incident light are positive.
 
• Distances measured against the direction of the incident light are negative.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Concave Mirror:**
 
 
• A concave mirror has a reflecting surface that curves inward, resembling the interior of a sphere.
 
• It forms real, inverted images when the object is beyond the focal point and virtual, upright images when the object is inside the focal point.
 
• Applications: Used in headlights, shaving mirrors, and astronomical telescopes.
 
 
 
• **Image Formation by Concave Mirrors:**
 
 
• If the object is placed:
 
 
• **Beyond the center of curvature:** Image is real, inverted, and smaller.
 
• **At the center of curvature:** Image is real, inverted, and of the same size.
 
• **Between the center of curvature and focus:** Image is real, inverted, and magnified.
 
• **At the focus:** Image is highly magnified and formed at infinity.
 
• **Between the focus and the pole:** Image is virtual, upright, and magnified.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Sign Conventions in Mirrors:**
 
 
• **Object distance (u):** Always negative for real objects.
 
• **Image distance (v):** Positive for real images and negative for virtual images.
 
• **Focal length (f):** Negative for concave mirrors and positive for convex mirrors.

questions.question: An electric bulb is rated 110 Watt – 220 Volt. The current drawn by the bulb is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.5 A**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The power rating of the electric bulb is given as **110 Watt**, and the voltage rating is **220 Volt**.
 
• The formula for current is derived from the basic formula of power: **P = V × I**, where:
 
 
• P = Power (in Watts)
 
• V = Voltage (in Volts)
 
• I = Current (in Amperes)
 
 
 
• Rearranging the formula to find the current gives: **I = P / V**.
 
• Substituting the given values:
 
 
• P = 110 W
 
• V = 220 V
 
 **I = 110 / 220 = 0.5 A**.
 
• **Hence, the current drawn by the bulb is 0.5 A.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Electric Power:**

 
 
• **Power** is the rate at which electrical energy is transferred by an electric circuit.
 
• It is measured in **Watts (W)**, where 1 Watt = 1 Joule/second.
 
• The formula for power in an electrical circuit is: **P = V × I**, where P is power, V is voltage, and I is current.
 
 
 
• **Voltage:**
 
 
• **Voltage** is the electrical potential difference between two points in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **Volts (V)**, and it represents the energy per unit charge.
 
 
 
• **Current:**
 
 
• **Current** is the flow of electric charge in a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **Amperes (A)**, where 1 Ampere = 1 Coulomb/second.
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:**
 
 
• According to Ohm's Law, **V = I × R**, where V is voltage, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This relationship helps in determining the behavior of electrical circuits.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• The calculation of current is essential for determining the efficiency and safety of electrical appliances.
 
• It helps in designing circuits and selecting appropriate fuses or circuit breakers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Practical Example:**

 
 
• If a bulb with the same rating (110 W, 220 V) is connected to a lower voltage source, the current drawn will decrease proportionally.
 
• For example, if the voltage is halved to 110 V, the current will also reduce to **0.25 A**.
 
 
 
• **Safety Measures:**
 
 
• Always ensure that the voltage supply matches the rated voltage of the appliance to avoid damage or inefficiency.
 
• Using appliances at incorrect voltage can lead to overheating, reduced lifespan, or even short circuits.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements are correct about molecular mass?

Statement 1: The molecular mass of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule of the substance.

Statement 2: It is also known as the relative mass of a molecule.

Statement 3: It is expressed in atomic mass units (u).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Statements 1, 2, and 3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Statement 1:** The molecular mass of a substance is the sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in a molecule of the substance.

 
 
• This statement is **correct**. Molecular mass is calculated by adding up the atomic masses of all the constituent atoms in a molecule. For example, the molecular mass of water (H₂O) is calculated as:

 
 
• Atomic mass of hydrogen = 1 u (2 atoms of H contribute 2 u)
 
• Atomic mass of oxygen = 16 u
 
• Total molecular mass = 2 + 16 = 18 u
 
 
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** It is also known as the relative mass of a molecule.
 
 
• This statement is **correct**. The molecular mass is often referred to as the relative molecular mass because it compares the mass of a molecule to 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom. This concept is widely used in chemistry.
 
 
 
• **Statement 3:** It is expressed in atomic mass units (u).
 
 
• This statement is **correct**. The molecular mass is expressed in atomic mass units (u), where 1 u is defined as 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom. For example, the molecular mass of CO₂ (carbon dioxide) is 44 u.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atomic Mass:**

 
 
• The atomic mass of an element is the mass of a single atom of that element, expressed in atomic mass units (u).
 
• For example, the atomic mass of hydrogen is approximately 1 u, while that of oxygen is approximately 16 u.
 
 
 
• **Molecular Mass Calculation:**
 
 
• To calculate the molecular mass, sum up the atomic masses of all the constituent atoms in the molecule. For example:
 
 
• For CH₄ (methane): Molecular mass = (1 × 12) + (4 × 1) = 16 u
 
• For H₂SO₄ (sulfuric acid): Molecular mass = (2 × 1) + (1 × 32) + (4 × 16) = 98 u
 
 
 
 
 
• **Relative Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• The term "relative molecular mass" is interchangeable with molecular mass and compares the mass of a molecule to 1/12th the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
 
• It is a dimensionless quantity and is numerically equal to the molecular mass expressed in atomic mass units (u).
 
 
 
• **Importance of Molecular Mass:**
 
 
• Molecular mass is essential in stoichiometric calculations, chemical reactions, and understanding molecular structures.
 
• It helps in determining the proportions of elements in a compound and predicting the quantities of reactants and products in a reaction.
 
 
 
• **Units of Measurement:**
 
 
• Molecular mass is measured in atomic mass units (u), where 1 u = 1.66053906660 × 10⁻²⁷ kg.
 
• Mass spectrometry is often used to measure molecular mass precisely in laboratories.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Atomic Mass Unit (u):**

 
 
• The atomic mass unit is a standard unit of mass used to express atomic and molecular masses.
 
• It is defined as 1/12th the mass of a single atom of carbon-12 (C-12).
 
 
 
• **Avogadro's Number:**
 
 
• Avogadro's number (6.022 × 10²³) relates the atomic or molecular mass of a substance to the number of atoms or molecules in a mole.
 
• This concept is crucial in understanding the relationship between macroscopic and microscopic properties of matter.
 
 
 
• **Applications:**
 
 
• Molecular mass is widely used in chemistry for determining molar masses, stoichiometric ratios, and solution concentrations.
 
• It is also essential in biochemistry for understanding the structure and function of biomolecules like proteins, DNA, and enzymes.

questions.question: Which of the following methods is an example of asexual reproduction in plants?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vegetative Propagation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Vegetative propagation** is a form of **asexual reproduction** in plants, where new plants grow from vegetative parts such as roots, stems, or leaves rather than seeds.
 
• This method does not involve the fusion of gametes, which is a characteristic of sexual reproduction.
 
• Examples of vegetative propagation include the growth of plants like **potatoes** from tubers, **onions** from bulbs, and **strawberries** from runners.
 
• It allows plants to reproduce quickly and maintain genetic uniformity, as the offspring are identical to the parent plant.
 
• Some common artificial methods of vegetative propagation include **grafting, layering, and tissue culture**, which are widely used in agriculture and horticulture to propagate desirable plant varieties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pollination:**

 
 
• **Pollination** is the process of transferring pollen grains from the male anther to the female stigma of a flower, leading to fertilization.
 
• It is a part of **sexual reproduction** in plants and involves the formation of seeds.
 
• Pollination can occur through various agents such as **wind, water, insects, birds, or animals**.
 
• *Hence, this option is incorrect as it is not a method of asexual reproduction.*
 
 
 
• **Fertilization:**
 
 
• Fertilization is the fusion of male and female gametes to form a zygote, which then develops into a seed.
 
• It is a key process in **sexual reproduction** in plants.
 
• *Therefore, this option is incorrect for asexual reproduction.*
 
 
 
• **Germination:**
 
 
• **Germination** is the process by which a seed develops into a new plant under favorable conditions.
 
• It is a subsequent stage of sexual reproduction, dependent on seed formation.
 
• *Thus, this option is not related to asexual reproduction.*
 
 
 
• **Examples of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• **Natural methods:** Runners in **strawberries**, tubers in **potatoes**, bulbs in **onions**, and rhizomes in **ginger**.
 
• **Artificial methods:** **Grafting** (e.g., mango), **cutting** (e.g., rose), **layering** (e.g., jasmine), and **tissue culture** (e.g., orchids).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Vegetative Propagation:**

 
 
• Preserves **genetic uniformity**, as offspring are clones of the parent plant.
 
• Allows for the propagation of plants that do not produce viable seeds or have long seed dormancy periods.
 
• Speeds up plant reproduction compared to seed-based methods.
 
 
 
• **Disadvantages of Vegetative Propagation:**
 
 
• Does not promote **genetic diversity**, making plants vulnerable to diseases and environmental changes.
 
• May require specialized skills or equipment, especially in artificial propagation methods like tissue culture.

questions.question: Which of the following reproductive method will generate greater diversity in population?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sexual Reproduction**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• **Sexual reproduction** involves the fusion of male and female gametes (sperm and egg), resulting in the formation of offspring with genetic material from both parents. 
 
• This process leads to **genetic recombination**, which creates new combinations of genes, thereby increasing genetic diversity in the population. 
 
• It enables populations to adapt better to changing environments, as greater genetic variation increases the likelihood of individuals possessing traits that enhance survival and reproduction. 
 
• Unlike asexual reproduction methods like fragmentation, budding, or binary fission, sexual reproduction does not produce clones, thus avoiding the risk of accumulating harmful mutations over generations. 
 
• Examples of organisms reproducing sexually include humans, animals, flowering plants, and some fungi. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Fragmentation:** 
 
• Fragmentation is a form of asexual reproduction where an organism splits into fragments, and each fragment grows into a new, genetically identical organism. 
 
• Examples: Spirogyra (a type of algae) and some flatworms. 
 
• While it is a quick way to reproduce, it results in no genetic variation, as offspring are clones of the parent. 
 
 

 
• **Budding:** 
 
• Budding is another asexual method where a new organism develops from an outgrowth or bud on the parent organism. 
 
• Examples: Yeast, hydra, and some species of coral. 
 
• Like fragmentation, it produces genetically identical offspring, limiting genetic diversity. 
 
 

 
• **Binary Fission:** 
 
• Binary fission is an asexual reproductive process where a single organism divides into two identical daughter cells. 
 
• It is common in prokaryotic organisms like bacteria and some protozoa. 
 
• This method is efficient but does not contribute to genetic diversity. 
 
 

 
• **Sexual Reproduction:** 
 
• Sexual reproduction is the process where genetic material from two parents combines to produce genetically distinct offspring. 
 
• It involves processes such as meiosis (formation of haploid gametes) and fertilization (fusion of gametes). 
 
• This method is common in animals, plants, and fungi and is essential for evolution and adaptation. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Advantages of sexual reproduction:** 
 
• Promotes **genetic diversity**, which is crucial for adaptation and survival in changing environments. 
 
• Allows for the elimination of harmful mutations over generations. 
 
• Facilitates species evolution by introducing new gene combinations. 
 
 

 
• **Limitations of asexual reproduction:** 
 
• Lack of genetic diversity can make populations vulnerable to environmental changes, diseases, and other challenges. 
 
• Organisms are exact clones, so any genetic defect in the parent is passed on to the offspring. 
 
 

 
• **Adaptation and Evolution:** 
 
• Sexual reproduction is a driving force behind the process of evolution, as it facilitates natural selection by producing varied traits in offspring. 
 
• Populations with greater genetic diversity are better equipped to adapt to new environmental pressures, such as climate change or emerging diseases.

__

questions.question: Why do we experience muscle cramps after heavy exercise?

options.text: Due to accumulation of lactic acid
Because blood flow completely stops during exercise
Due to a decrease in body temperature

The correct answer is __**Due to accumulation of lactic acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muscle cramps after heavy exercise** occur primarily due to the **accumulation of lactic acid** in the muscles. Lactic acid is a by-product of anaerobic respiration, which happens when the oxygen supply to the muscles is insufficient during intense physical activities.
 
• When muscles perform strenuous exercise, they may switch to **anaerobic metabolism**, leading to the buildup of lactic acid. This causes a **drop in pH levels** in the muscle tissue, resulting in a burning sensation and cramps.
 
• **Insufficient oxygen supply:** During vigorous physical activities, muscles require more oxygen. If the supply is inadequate, the muscles rely on anaerobic respiration, which produces lactic acid.
 
• The accumulation of lactic acid affects the **nerve endings** in the muscles, causing discomfort and cramping sensations. This phenomenon is temporary and typically resolves once the lactic acid is flushed out of the system.
 
• Proper **hydration and stretching** before and after exercise can help reduce the risk of muscle cramps caused by lactic acid buildup.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Anaerobic respiration:**

 
 
• Occurs when oxygen levels are insufficient for aerobic respiration.
 
• Produces energy for muscle contraction but generates **lactic acid** as a by-product.
 
• Lactic acid buildup leads to temporary muscle fatigue and cramps.
 
 
 
• **Role of lactic acid:**
 
 
• Lactic acid is cleared from the muscles and metabolized into glucose by the **liver** through a process called the **Cori cycle**.
 
• The buildup of lactic acid can lead to a **temporary decrease in muscle efficiency**.
 
 
 
• **Preventing muscle cramps:**
 
 
• Maintain proper **hydration** during and after exercise to reduce the risk of cramps.
 
• Include **electrolytes** in your diet to ensure muscle function and avoid electrolyte imbalance.
 
• Perform **warm-up and cool-down exercises** to improve blood circulation and reduce lactic acid buildup.
 
 
 
• **Misconceptions:**
 
 
• Muscle cramps are not caused by the complete cessation of blood flow (**Statement 3 is incorrect**). Blood flow increases during exercise to supply oxygen to the muscles.
 
• Muscle cramps are not due to a decrease in body temperature (**Statement 4 is incorrect**). Body temperature typically rises during exercise.
 
• Muscles do not stop contracting during cramps (**Statement 2 is incorrect**). On the contrary, cramps are due to involuntary contractions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Lactic acid threshold:** This refers to the exercise intensity at which lactic acid starts accumulating significantly in the muscles. Training at or below this threshold can improve endurance.
 
• **Electrolyte imbalance:** Lack of electrolytes like sodium, potassium, and magnesium can exacerbate muscle cramps. Proper nutrition is essential for maintaining muscle function.
 
• **Stretching and massage:** Post-exercise stretching and massage can help in dissipating lactic acid and relieving cramps.
 
• **Scientific studies:** Research has shown that lactic acid is rapidly cleared from the muscles after exercise, and cramps are generally resolved within a short duration.

__
 
• The **plasma membrane**, also known as the **cell membrane**, is referred to as **selectively permeable** because it allows only specific substances to enter or leave the cell, while blocking others. This selective permeability ensures the maintenance of the cell's internal environment.
 
• This selective nature is attributed to the **phospholipid bilayer** structure of the membrane, which is embedded with proteins. Small and non-polar molecules, like oxygen and carbon dioxide, can pass through easily, while larger or charged molecules require specific transport mechanisms.
 
• Transport across the membrane occurs in two forms: **passive transport** (e.g., diffusion and osmosis, which do not require energy) and **active transport** (which uses energy to move substances against their concentration gradient).
 
• The plasma membrane also contains **protein channels and carriers** that facilitate the transport of larger or charged molecules, such as glucose and ions, ensuring that only the necessary substances enter or exit the cell.
 
• This selective permeability plays a critical role in processes like **homeostasis**, allowing the cell to maintain a stable internal environment despite changes in the external surroundings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Components of the Plasma Membrane:**

 
 
• The plasma membrane is composed of a **phospholipid bilayer**, where the hydrophilic (water-attracting) heads face outward and the hydrophobic (water-repelling) tails face inward.
 
• **Embedded proteins:** These include integral and peripheral proteins, which assist in transport, signal transduction, and cell recognition.
 
• **Cholesterol:** Cholesterol molecules are interspersed within the bilayer, providing stability and fluidity to the membrane.
 
• **Carbohydrates:** Found attached to proteins or lipids on the extracellular side of the membrane, they play a role in cell-cell recognition and signaling.
 
 
 
• **Mechanisms of Transport:**
 
 
• **Passive Transport:** Includes **diffusion** (movement of molecules from high to low concentration), **osmosis** (diffusion of water), and **facilitated diffusion** (movement of molecules via specific protein channels).
 
• **Active Transport:** Requires energy in the form of ATP to transport substances against their concentration gradient. Examples include the **sodium-potassium pump**.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Selective Permeability:**
 
 
• Helps maintain a stable **internal environment (homeostasis)** by regulating ion concentrations, pH levels, and nutrient intake.
 
• Facilitates communication between cells through the exchange of signaling molecules.
 
• Protects the cell from harmful substances and toxins by restricting their entry.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Substances and Their Transport:**
 
 
• **Small, non-polar molecules:** Oxygen (O₂) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) diffuse freely across the membrane.
 
• **Large molecules:** Glucose and amino acids require protein carriers or channels for transport.
 
• **Ions:** Sodium (Na⁺), potassium (K⁺), and calcium (Ca²⁺) move through specific ion channels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fluid Mosaic Model:** Proposed by **Singer and Nicolson in 1972**, this model describes the plasma membrane as a fluid structure with various proteins floating in or on the lipid bilayer.
 
• **Endocytosis and Exocytosis:** These processes allow the cell to engulf large particles (endocytosis) or release substances (exocytosis) by forming vesicles.
 
• **Diseases Related to Membrane Dysfunction:** Disorders like **Cystic Fibrosis** occur due to faulty ion channels in the plasma membrane.
 
• **Role in Cell Communication:** Membrane proteins act as receptors for hormones, neurotransmitters, and other signaling molecules, enabling intercellular communication.

questions.question: In May 2025, which among the following institutions formally announced the creation of the Payments Regulatory Board (PRB), a six-member panel responsible for overseeing the country’s payment systems?

questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** announced the formation of the **Payments Regulatory Board (PRB)** in May 2025. The PRB is a six-member panel entrusted with the responsibility of overseeing and regulating the country's payment systems.
 
• The **Payments Regulatory Board** was established as per the recommendations of the **Committee on Digital Payments**, headed by **Ratan Watal**. This committee emphasized the need for a separate regulatory body for payment systems in India.
 
• The PRB's objectives include ensuring the development of secure, efficient, and accessible payment systems while promoting innovation and competition in the payment ecosystem.
 
• The six-member PRB comprises the **Governor of the RBI** as the Chairperson, a Deputy Governor of the RBI as a member, and nominees from the Central Government, along with independent experts in the field of payment systems.
 
• The establishment of the PRB aligns with the RBI's role in fostering a robust and secure digital payment infrastructure, which is critical for the country's digital economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**

 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India** is India's central bank, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai**, Maharashtra, and primarily functions to regulate the issue of currency and manage the country's monetary policy.
 
• The RBI plays a crucial role in supervising and regulating banks, fostering financial stability, and promoting the development of financial markets.
 
 
 
• **Committee on Digital Payments:**
 
 
• The **Ratan Watal Committee** was constituted by the Government of India in **2016** to suggest measures to increase the use of digital payments.
 
• It recommended the establishment of a dedicated regulatory body for payment systems to ensure better governance and oversight.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Payments Regulatory Board:**
 
 
• Regulating payment systems in India to ensure their security, efficiency, and accessibility.
 
• Promoting competition and innovation in the payment ecosystem.
 
• Ensuring the protection of consumer interests in the digital payment space.
 
• Monitoring the compliance of payment service providers with regulatory norms and guidelines.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Payment Systems Regulation:**
 
 
• A robust payment system infrastructure ensures **secure and efficient transactions**, fostering trust in the digital economy.
 
• Regulation helps in mitigating risks such as **frauds, cyberattacks, and operational failures** in payment systems.
 
• It promotes financial inclusion by enabling easier access to digital payment methods for underserved populations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The RBI is responsible for overseeing the country's payment systems under the **Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007**.
 
• The establishment of the PRB was a significant step to ensure the growth of a **secure, seamless, and innovative payment ecosystem** in India.
 
• The PRB's formation reflects India's commitment to strengthening its digital payment infrastructure, which is pivotal to achieving a **cashless economy**.
 
• Global examples, such as the **Payment Systems Regulator (PSR)** in the UK, have demonstrated the benefits of having a separate regulatory body for payment systems.

• Dhaki drummers play a pivotal role in enhancing the spiritual experience of the festival through their vibrant and energetic beats.

questions.question: In 2025, Shubhanshu Shukla conducted an International Space Station (ISS) experiment with moong and methi seeds to study:

options.text: Soil nutrient cycling under space conditions
Resistance of legumes to common pesticides

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Seed germination under microgravity conditions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seed germination under microgravity conditions** was the focus of Shubhanshu Shukla's experiment in 2025 on the International Space Station (ISS).
 
• The study aimed to understand how seeds like **moong** (green gram) and **methi** (fenugreek) germinate in the absence of Earth's gravity.
 
• Microgravity poses unique challenges for biological processes such as seed germination, including issues like **water distribution, nutrient absorption, and root growth orientation**.
 
• Understanding seed behavior in space is critical for the development of **space farming**, a necessary step for long-term human space exploration and colonization.
 
• This experiment contributes to the field of astrobiology and sheds light on the viability of growing food in extraterrestrial environments. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Microgravity and Its Effects:**

 
 
• Microgravity is a condition where objects appear to be weightless and experience minimal gravitational force. It is common in space.
 
• Under microgravity, water tends to form spherical droplets, and nutrient distribution becomes uneven, which can complicate plant growth.
 
 
 
• **Space Farming:**
 
 
• Space farming involves growing crops in extraterrestrial environments, such as the ISS or other planets like Mars.
 
• It is essential for providing a sustainable source of food for astronauts on long-duration missions.
 
• Plants also contribute to life support systems by producing oxygen and removing carbon dioxide.
 
 
 
• **Moong and Methi Seeds:**
 
 
• **Moong** (green gram) is a protein-rich legume widely used in Indian cuisine.
 
• **Methi** (fenugreek) is known for its nutritional and medicinal properties, including its ability to reduce blood sugar levels.
 
• Both are fast-growing plants, making them ideal for short-term experiments like those conducted on the ISS.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Seed Germination Studies in Space:**
 
 
• Understanding seed germination in space helps scientists design systems for growing crops in extraterrestrial environments.
 
• It also contributes to our understanding of how plants adapt to extreme conditions, which can have applications on Earth, such as in arid or nutrient-poor soils.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Challenges in Space Farming:**

 
 
• Watering plants in microgravity is difficult as water does not flow naturally but instead forms floating droplets.
 
• Lack of soil in space requires innovative techniques like hydroponics or aeroponics for plant growth.
 
• Light exposure in spacecraft is artificial, requiring the use of LED systems to simulate sunlight.
 
 
 
• **Previous Experiments:**
 
 
• NASA has conducted experiments on growing crops like lettuce, radishes, and wheat aboard the ISS.
 
• The European Space Agency (ESA) has also studied plant growth under simulated Martian and lunar conditions.
 
 
 
• **Future Implications:**
 
 
• Successful space farming can reduce the dependency on Earth for food supplies during space missions.
 
• It can also pave the way for establishing self-sustaining human colonies on planets like Mars.

questions.question: What is the main aim of the Youth Spiritual Summit held in Varanasi on the banks of River Ganga in July 2025?

options.text: Encourage use of digital tools for literacy
Foster a national resolve against drug abuse
Support local youth in rural entrepreneurship

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Foster a national resolve against drug abuse**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Youth Spiritual Summit** held in **Varanasi** on the banks of the **River Ganga** in **July 2025** aimed to address a critical social issue of drug abuse, fostering awareness and collective resolve among the youth.
 
• The summit emphasized the importance of **spiritual and moral education** as a tool to combat the growing menace of drug addiction, particularly among young individuals in India.
 
• It was organized with the collaboration of various **governmental, non-governmental, and spiritual organizations**, bringing together youth leaders, educators, and policymakers to discuss strategies for tackling substance abuse.
 
• Participants were encouraged to adopt a lifestyle rooted in **values, discipline, and mindfulness** to resist the temptation of drugs and promote overall well-being.
 
• The initiative aligns with the Indian Government's broader mission to achieve a **drug-free society** and support youth in becoming responsible citizens contributing positively to national development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Drug Abuse in India:**

 
 
• Drug abuse is a major issue in India, with a significant portion of the youth population being affected. According to the **National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC) survey of 2019**, approximately **2.8% of the population** is engaged in opioid use.
 
• Drugs like **heroin, cannabis, and prescription drugs** are among the most abused substances in the country.
 
• The issue is exacerbated by factors such as **peer pressure, unemployment, stress, and lack of awareness**.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives to Combat Drug Abuse:**
 
 
• The Indian Government has launched programs like the **National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR) 2018-2025** to prevent drug abuse and ensure the rehabilitation of affected individuals.
 
• Anti-drug campaigns such as **Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyan** focus on creating awareness and providing support at the grassroots level.
 
• Collaboration with international organizations like the **United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC)** is also in place to address the issue globally.
 
 
 
• **Spiritual and Moral Education:**
 
 
• Spiritual practices like **yoga, meditation, and mindfulness** play a vital role in helping individuals overcome addiction by promoting mental clarity and emotional stability.
 
• Many **rehabilitation centers** in India incorporate spiritual teachings to aid in the recovery process.
 
• Spiritual summits provide a platform for the youth to engage with thought leaders and adopt healthier lifestyles.
 
 
 
• **Role of Youth in Tackling Drug Abuse:**
 
 
• Youth represent the future of the nation and play a critical role in spreading awareness and advocating for a drug-free society.
 
• Peer-led initiatives and community programs organized by youth groups have proven effective in reducing drug abuse in local communities.
 
• Participation in summits like the **Youth Spiritual Summit** empowers young individuals to lead by example and inspire others to avoid substance abuse.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Varanasi:**

 
 
• Varanasi, located on the banks of the **River Ganga**, is one of the most sacred cities in India and serves as an ideal location for hosting spiritual events.
 
• The city's historical and cultural heritage aligns with the themes of spirituality and moral upliftment promoted during the summit.
 
 
 
• **Global Perspective on Drug Abuse:**
 
 
• The **World Drug Report 2023** by the **United Nations** states that around **284 million people** aged 15-64 used drugs globally in 2020.
 
• Efforts to combat drug abuse often require international cooperation and the implementation of evidence-based policies.
 
 
 
• **Key Challenges:**
 
 
• Lack of awareness about the harmful effects of drugs and inadequate access to rehabilitation services are major barriers to tackling drug abuse.
 
• Social stigma associated with addiction often prevents individuals from seeking help.

questions.question: In February 2025, the Technology Development Board signed an agreement with which company to produce purified pyrolysis oil to make circular plastics and sustainable chemicals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**APChemi Pvt. Ltd, Navi Mumbai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Technology Development Board (TDB)** signed an agreement with **APChemi Pvt. Ltd., Navi Mumbai**, in **February 2025** to produce purified pyrolysis oil for making circular plastics and sustainable chemicals.
 
• **APChemi Pvt. Ltd.** specializes in converting waste plastics into **high-value pyrolysis oil**, which can be further refined into sustainable chemicals and circular plastics.
 
• The collaboration aims to bolster the **circular economy** by promoting the reuse of plastic waste, reducing environmental pollution, and supporting sustainable industrial practices.
 
• Purified pyrolysis oil is a critical feedstock for creating **low-carbon plastics** and sustainable chemical solutions, aligning with India’s **green and environmental goals**.
 
• Through this agreement, the initiative aims to reduce the dependency on fossil fuel-based feedstocks in the production of plastics and chemicals, promoting the use of **recycled materials**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **APChemi Pvt. Ltd.**:

 
 
• Headquartered in **Navi Mumbai**, this company is a leading technology provider in the field of **waste plastic pyrolysis**.
 
• It operates advanced pyrolysis facilities that transform **non-recyclable plastic waste** into purified pyrolysis oil, which can be used in various industrial applications.
 
• APChemi has gained recognition for its **cutting-edge technology** and its commitment to sustainability and reducing plastic waste.
 
 
 
• **Technology Development Board (TDB):**
 
 
• The **Technology Development Board** is a statutory body under the **Department of Science and Technology, Government of India**.
 
• Its primary mission is to promote the development and commercialization of indigenous technology solutions in India.
 
• It provides financial assistance to industries and enterprises for innovative and environmentally sustainable projects.
 
 
 
• **Pyrolysis Technology:**
 
 
• Pyrolysis is a **thermal decomposition** process that converts organic materials, such as plastic waste, into useful by-products like **pyrolysis oil**, char, and syngas.
 
• The process operates at high temperatures in the absence of oxygen, ensuring that the materials break down into smaller molecules.
 
• Purified pyrolysis oil is increasingly being used as a **feedstock** for producing sustainable chemicals and circular plastics.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Circular Plastics:**
 
 
• Circular plastics are produced from recycled materials or sustainable feedstocks, reducing reliance on **virgin plastics** derived from fossil fuels.
 
• This approach helps in mitigating **plastic pollution** and contributes to achieving **climate goals** by lowering greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The use of circular plastics supports the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, particularly those related to responsible consumption and production.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Options Explained:**

 
 
• **Tata Chemicals Ltd., Mumbai:** Known for its chemical and specialty products, it focuses on industrial chemicals, agricultural solutions, and consumer products but is not directly involved in pyrolysis oil production.
 
• **Jaypee Chemicals, Jaipur:** Primarily engaged in the manufacture of basic chemicals but does not specialize in sustainable plastics or pyrolysis technologies.
 
• **Adani Chemicals Ltd., Ahmedabad:** Part of the Adani Group, focusing on fertilizers and industrial chemicals, but not directly linked to purified pyrolysis oil production.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:** The collaboration between TDB and APChemi addresses one of the most pressing environmental challenges—plastic waste management—by promoting recycling and sustainable practices.
 
• **Global Context:** The agreement reflects India’s commitment to the global shift towards a **circular economy** and aligns with **international efforts** to combat plastic pollution and climate change.

questions.question: With which country did India sign a significant defence Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) (through the JCBL Group) in April 2025 which is aimed at bolstering India’s domestic defence manufacturing capabilities?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Slovakia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **April 2025**, India signed a significant **defence Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** with **Slovakia**, facilitated through the **JCBL Group**.
 
• The agreement aims to **bolster India’s domestic defence manufacturing capabilities**, aligning with the "Make in India" initiative, which focuses on reducing dependency on imports and enhancing indigenous production.
 
• **Slovakia**, a prominent player in the defence manufacturing sector, is known for its advanced technologies in military equipment, including **armoured vehicles, artillery systems, and missile technologies**.
 
• This collaboration is expected to lead to the **transfer of technology (ToT), joint ventures, and skill enhancement** for Indian defence manufacturers, further boosting India’s self-reliance in defence production.
 
• The partnership highlights the growing importance of **international collaborations** in enhancing India’s strategic defence capabilities and fulfilling its vision of becoming a global defence export hub.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India’s Defence Manufacturing Sector:**

 
 
• The Indian government has introduced several reforms to promote **indigenous defence production**, such as increasing the **FDI limit to 74%** through the automatic route.
 
• Key initiatives like **‘Atmanirbhar Bharat’** and the **Defence Production and Export Promotion Policy (DPEPP) 2020** aim to enhance the domestic defence manufacturing ecosystem.
 
• India’s defence exports have witnessed a significant rise, with the government targeting **₹35,000 crores in exports by 2025**.
 
 
 
• **Slovakia’s Defence Industry:**
 
 
• Slovakia is renowned for its expertise in manufacturing **land-based defence systems**, including **infantry fighting vehicles, mortars, and radar systems**.
 
• The country is a member of **NATO** and the **European Union**, which ensures that its defence manufacturing standards align with global benchmarks.
 
• Slovakia’s defence exports are primarily focused on Europe, the Middle East, and now, emerging markets like India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of India-Slovakia Defence MoU:**
 
 
• The agreement is expected to enhance **India’s technological capabilities** in the defence sector by accessing Slovakia’s advanced military technologies.
 
• It provides a platform for **joint development and production**, ensuring that India can cater to its defence needs while also contributing to global markets.
 
• The partnership signifies India’s growing focus on establishing **strategic collaborations** with European nations to diversify its defence partnerships.
 
 
 
• **JCBL Group:**
 
 
• The **JCBL Group**, a leading Indian company, specializes in **automotive and defence manufacturing**, including armoured vehicles and other military hardware.
 
• The group has been instrumental in facilitating international collaborations to bring advanced technologies to India.
 
• Its role in this MoU underscores the importance of public-private partnerships in achieving India’s defence production goals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **‘Make in India’ Initiative:**

 
 
• Launched in **2014**, this initiative aims to transform India into a global manufacturing hub by encouraging both foreign and domestic companies to manufacture in India.
 
• In the defence sector, it emphasizes **self-reliance**, with policies designed to reduce imports and promote indigenous development.
 
• As part of this initiative, the government has identified **101 defence items** for indigenization.
 
 
 
• **Defence Collaboration with Other Nations:**
 
 
• India has signed similar defence agreements with countries like **Israel** (for UAVs and radar systems) and **Russia** (for BrahMos missile systems).
 
• These partnerships have significantly contributed to India’s defence capabilities and export potential.
